articles.body: Asian Games 2026 Live: Another medal event coming up for India After Abhay Singh’s silver-medal finish, the focus now shifts to the women’s singles gold-medal squash match. India’s Anahat Singh takes on Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam, with both players beginning the final level at 0–0. The match is scheduled to get underway next at Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena, as Anahat bids to add another squash medal for India..Asian Games 2026 Live: Abhay Singh secures the silver medal in the men’s singles event Abhay Singh secures the silver medal in the men’s singles event after going down 0–3 to Malaysia’s Ng Eain Yow in the gold-medal match. Ng takes the contest 11–9, 11–5, 11–5, while Abhay finishes with a hard-earned silver for India..Asian Games 2026 Live: Abhay Singh now under pressure Ng Eain Yow responds to Abhay Singh’s early charge and now leads 6–5 in the third game. Abhay remains within one point, but the Malaysian is once again edging ahead as he looks to close out the match with a 3–0 scoreline..Asian Games 2026 Live: Abhay Singh takes early lead in the third game Abhay Singh comes out firing in the third game and takes an early 4–2 lead over Ng Eain Yow. After dropping the first two games, the Indian is showing signs of a fightback as he looks to extend the men’s singles gold-medal match..Asian Games 2026 Live: Abhay Singh loses second game too Ng Eain Yow takes the second game 11–5 and moves 2–0 ahead of Abhay Singh in the men’s singles gold-medal match. Abhay now faces a difficult task, needing to win the next three games to turn the final around..Asian Games 2026 Live: India take on Vietnam in volleyball India edge past Vietnam 25-23 in a closely fought opening set to take a 1-0 lead. Jerome Vinith leads India’s attack with seven points, including several effective spikes, but Vietnam are proving to be a tough opponent and keeping the pressure on throughout the set..Asian Games 2026 Live: Abhay Singh loses the first game Ng Eain Yow takes the opening game 11–9 against Abhay Singh. The Malaysian makes the early breakthrough in the men’s singles gold-medal match, with Abhay now needing to respond in the second game. .Asian Games 2026 Live: Abhay Singh in men's singles squash final A brilliant piece of presence of mind from Abhay Singh! With Ng Eain Yow expecting the shot to go one way, Abhay changes the angle at the very last moment to catch his opponent off guard. The Indian stays right in the contest, with Ng leading 8–7 in the opening game..Asian Games 2026 Live: Abhay stays within touching distance Ng Eain Yow maintains his lead over Abhay Singh in the opening game of the men’s singles gold-medal match, moving 6–5 ahead. Abhay stays within touching distance as the Malaysian continues to hold a narrow advantage..Asian Games 2026 Live: An intense start to the competition In the opening game, Malaysia’s Ng Eain Yow leads India’s Abhay Singh 4–3 in the men’s singles gold-medal match. It is an early advantage for Ng, but Abhay remains within one point as the contest continues..Asian Games 2026 Live: Men’s singles squash final about to begin Indian squash begins a big Sunday with Abhay Singh taking on Malaysia’s Ng Eain Yow in the men’s singles gold-medal match. Ng, ranked 17th in the world, faces world No. 26 Abhay in a contest between the top two seeds, with both players having progressed through the tournament without major difficulty. Abhay also carries forward India’s strong tradition in men’s singles at the Asian Games, following in the footsteps of Saurav Ghosal. With a gold medal now within reach, Abhay looks to complete a campaign that could add another major chapter to India’s squash history..Asian Games 2026 Live: India suffer a 0-2 defeat against the Philippines in their women’s doubles Group B match India suffer a 0-2 defeat against the Philippines in their women’s doubles Group B match, losing 12-15, 6-15. It is India’s second defeat in the group stage, leaving them at the bottom of the standings for now..Asian Games 2026 Live: A gold-medal match coming up next India’s Abhay Singh takes on Malaysia’s Ng Eain Yow in the men’s singles gold-medal match at the Asian Games..Asian Games 2026 Live: Harjinder Kaur finishes ninth in 69kg; North Korea’s Song Kuk Hyang sets a new women’s 69kg world record Harjinder Kaur has finished ninth in the women’s 69kg weightlifting event at the Asian Games after managing just one successful clean-and-jerk attempt of 110kg. She did not take her final attempt at 126kg, which was her personal best from the 2026 Commonwealth Games. Kaur finished with a combined total of 204kg, following her silver-medal performance at the Commonwealth Games, where she recorded 227kg. North Korea’s Song Kuk Hyang sets a new women’s 69kg world record with a total of 273kg at the Asian Games, improving on her previous mark of 270kg. She records 121kg in the snatch and 152kg in the clean and jerk to claim the gold medal, while Chinese Taipei’s Chen Wen-huei takes silver with 232kg and Bahrain’s Ingrid Grueso wins bronze with 229kg..Asian Games 2026 Live: Indian archers continue to impress India have secured semifinal spots in all three recurve team events at the Asian Games, with the men’s side defeating China 5–1 in the quarterfinals and the women’s team beating Chinese Taipei 6–0. The men’s, women’s and mixed recurve teams are now set to compete in the semifinals on October 2, while the compound individual events begin tomorrow..Asian Games 2026 Live: First part of women’s 25m pistol qualification done! India’s Esha Singh finishes sixth in the precision stage of the women’s 25m pistol qualification with 290-9x. Rahi Sarnobat and Manu Bhaker are 15th and 16th, respectively, with scores of 287-6x. India sits third in the women’s 25m pistol team final after the precision stage, scoring 864-21x. Republic of Korea leads with 870-34x, followed by China on 868-33x. However, it is not the final standings. In the women's 25m pistol at the Asian Games, Precision and Rapid Fire are the two parts of the qualification round. The rapid stage is scheduled for September 28. .Asian Games 2026 Live: All four Indian athletes in Kurash out in the opening round All four Indian athletes in Kurash lose their opening bouts and are knocked out of the Asian Games 2026..Asian Games 2026 Live: Indian archers in action shortly The recurve archery team quarterfinals are set to begin shortly, with India’s men taking on China and the women facing Chinese Taipei. The compound men’s, women’s and mixed teams have already booked their places in the semifinals, scheduled for September 30. India’s recurve mixed team has also advanced to the last four after beating Vietnam and will face Japan in the semifinals..Asian Games 2026 Live: Tejaswin Shankar impressive in decathlon pole vault In the decathlon pole vault, Tejaswin Shankar clears 4.30m, the second-best jump of his career, earning 702 points. Japan’s Yuma Maruyama leads the event with a 5.10m clearance, worth 941 points..Asian Games 2026 Live: No medal for PV Sindhu PV Sindhu bows out of the women’s singles quarterfinal after Chen Yu Fei wins the deciding game 21-10. Sindhu takes the opening game 21-11 but Chen fights back to win the next two 21-18, 21-10, ending India’s medal hopes in the event..Asian Games 2026 Live: Sindhu's medal chances worsen PV Sindhu trails Chen Yu Fei 10-18 in the deciding game of their women’s singles quarterfinal. Chen is now just three points away from sealing her place in the semifinals..Asian Games 2026 Live: Harjinder Kaur disappoints in women’s 69kg final Harjinder Kaur finishes the snatch section of the women’s 69kg final with a total of 94kg after failing with her final two attempts at 97kg. She is seven kilograms short of her personal best of 101kg, set in Glasgow earlier this year, and currently sits second-last in the standings..Asian Games 2026 Live: Sindhu needs a strong comeback PV Sindhu trails Chen Yu Fei 7-11 in the deciding game of their women’s singles quarterfinal. Chen maintains her four-point advantage as Sindhu looks to fight her way back into the contest..Asian Games 2026 Live: Medal chances get better in women’s 400m hurdles Anu Raghavan storms into the women’s 400m hurdles final with a personal best of 55.84 seconds. She joins compatriot Vithya Ramraj, giving India two finalists in the event..Asian Games 2026 Live: The early signs are this is going down to the wire PV Sindhu trails Chen Yu Fei 6-8 in the deciding game of their women’s singles quarterfinal. The Chinese shuttler holds a two-point lead as the contest remains closely fought..Asian Games 2026 Live: Sindhu trailing at the moment PV Sindhu falls behind Chen Yu Fei in the deciding game of their women’s singles quarterfinal. After splitting the first two games 21-11 and 18-21, Chen takes an early 5-2 lead in the decider..Asian Games 2026 Live: Sindhu vs Chen goes into decider It is 1-1 between PV Sindhu and Chen Yu Fei after two games. Sindhu takes the opening game 21-11, but Chen responds by winning the second 21-18. The quarterfinal now goes into a deciding third game..Asian Games 2026 Live: The Chinese takes back the lead over Sindhu in the second game Chen Yu Fei is back in front at 15-13 in the second game against PV Sindhu. Sindhu takes the opening game 21-11, but Chen is now leading the second as the quarterfinal remains closely contested..Asian Games 2026 Live: Day 1 of the Trap qualification concludes Day 1 of the Trap qualification concludes with Neeru leading the women’s field for India with 46 out of 50. Aashima Ahlawat is 16th on 42, while Manisha Keer sits 24th with 40. In the men’s qualification, Kynan Chenai is 11th with 47, Shapath Bharadwaj is 22nd with 45, and Ahvar Rizvi is 35th with 41. India’s teams are both seventh in their respective standings, with two more days of qualification remaining..Asian Games 2026 Live: PV Sindhu in good touch It’s all square at 9-9 in the second game between PV Sindhu and Chen Yu Fei. Sindhu has fought back strongly in the second game after giving away too many points earlier in the game. She took the opening game 21-11, with the quarterfinal finely poised. A win here means a medal secured for India. Sindhu remains the only person left in the fray from India's badminton contingent. Other have already been knocked out..Asian Games 2026 Live: Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh, and Rahi Sarnobat in women’s 25m pistol qualification The women’s 25m pistol qualification is underway, with the precision stage in progress. Esha Singh is currently seventh with 290 points, while Manu Bhaker sits 15th on 287 and Rahi Sarnobat is 20th with 238. India sits third in the women’s 25m pistol team final after the precision stage, with a score of 815-20x. Republic of Korea leads with 823-34x, followed by China on 820-30x, while Kazakhstan is fourth with 821-21x. The rapid stage is scheduled for September 28..Asian Games 2026 Live: PV Sindu takes the first game PV Sindhu takes the opening game 21-11 against China’s Chen Yu Fei in the women’s singles quarterfinal. Sindhu makes a strong start and moves one game away from keeping her medal hopes alive..Asian Games 2026 Live: Unnati Hooda loses, misses out on Asiad medal Unnati Hooda bows out of the women’s singles quarterfinal after Akane Yamaguchi wins the decider 21-17. Hooda fights back strongly after dropping the opening game 16-21, taking the second 21-14, but Yamaguchi holds her nerve in the final game to win 21-17 and advance to the semifinals..Asian Games 2026 Live: An intense decider between Unnati Hooda and Akane Yamaguchi It is an intense decider between Unnati Hooda and Akane Yamaguchi, with Hooda trailing 17-19. The Indian has already fought back from losing the opening game 16-21 by taking the second 21-14, and she is now three points away from a place in the semifinals..Asian Games 2026 Live: No medal in equestrian India finishes its equestrian campaign at the Asian Games 2026 without a medal. The country had won one gold and one bronze in the previous edition in 2022. Anush Agarwalla, who was part of India’s medal-winning individual and team efforts then, is not selected for the 2026 team..Asian Games 2026 Live: Ankush Panghal through to the semis Ankush Panghal wins the men’s 80kg quarterfinal against Nekruz Salimov by unanimous decision. He controls the contest across all three rounds to book his place in the semifinals, securing a coveted medal for India. The colour of the medal, however, is yet to be decided. .Asian Games 2026 Live: Ankush Panghal favourite to make it to the next round Ankush Panghal takes the second round 5-0 as well, maintaining his advantage over Nekruz Salimov in the men’s 80kg quarterfinal. Panghal continues to stay composed and active, giving himself a strong position heading into the final round. Earlier, Ankush took the opening round 5-0 against Nekruz Salimov in the men’s 80kg quarterfinal. Panghal stays active with quick jabs and movement, finding success with right hooks before landing a series of 1-2 combinations to the body. All five judges score the round 10-9 in Panghal’s favour across both rounds..Asian Games 2026 Live: Unnati Hooda takes the second game 21-14, forces the decider; a place in the semis on the line Unnati Hooda takes the second game 21-14 against Akane Yamaguchi to level the quarterfinal and force a decider. Hooda shows excellent composure and aggression, combining patient rallies with well-placed attacking shots before winning six points in a row to move 19-6 ahead. Yamaguchi cannot find a way back, and Hooda converts her first game point when the Japanese shuttler sends the return into the net..Asian Games 2026 Live: Sreeshankar, David advance to men's long jump final In the men’s long jump qualification, Sreeshankar and David secure their spots in the final with jumps of 7.84m and 7.62m, respectively, while Uzbekistan’s Anvar Anvarov leads the standings with an 8.00m effort..Asian Games 2026 Live: Unnati Hooda eyes semi-final berth Unnati Hooda faces a tough challenge against Japan's Akane Yamaguchi in the women's singles quarterfinal. The Indian teenager makes a positive start and stays level at 3-3, but Yamaguchi then pulls away with eight straight points. The Japanese shuttler takes an 11-4 lead into the interval, leaving Unnati with plenty of ground to make up in the remainder of the game..Asian Games 2026 Live: Vithya Ramraj into women's 400m hurdles final Vithya Ramraj advances to the women's 400m hurdles final after finishing second in her heat. She clocks 55.73 seconds, finishing behind Kazakhstan's Adelina Zems, who wins the heat in 55.29 seconds. Japan's Honoka Aoki takes third in 56.46 seconds. Vithya safely secures an automatic qualification spot for the final..Asian Games 2026 Live: Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh and Rahi Sarnobat in action Manu Bhaker, Esha Singh and Rahi Sarnobat are in action in the women's 25m pistol qualification, with the precision stage also counting towards the team event. The Indian trio will look to put together strong scores in the precision round as they aim to advance in the individual competition and build a solid position in the team standings..Asian Games 2026 Live: Tejaswin Shankar slips to third in decathlon standings Tejaswin Shankar has a difficult outing in the decathlon discus throw, recording 36.77m for 599 points. The effort sees him slip to third in the overall standings with 5,869 points. China's Chen Xinghua moves into the lead on 5,919 points, while Japan's Yuma Maruyama is second with 5,914. Tejaswin now heads into the pole vault and javelin, two events that pose another challenge in his bid to stay in medal contention..Asian Games 2026 Live: Santhosh Kumar Tamilarasan books his place in the men's 400m hurdles final Santhosh Kumar Tamilarasan books his place in the men's 400m hurdles final after finishing second in his heat. He clocks 49.61 seconds to secure one of the automatic qualification spots. India's Yashas Palaksha is set to compete in the second heat shortly, with another opportunity for the country to reach the final. Yashas Palaksha is unable to complete his men's 400m hurdles heat after pulling up just before the first hurdle. As a result, Santhosh Kumar Tamilarasan is India's only finalist in the event. Santhosh advances after finishing second in his heat with 49.61 seconds, which ranks him as the third-fastest qualifier overall from the heats..Asian Games 2026 Live: Class topper, wooden gun, Nano rides: How Shapath Bharadwaj found his way to the Asian Games - READ HERE Class topper Shapath Bharadwaj fell in love with shooting at nine after watching his elder brother train. His father, S Raju, supported the dream, even getting a carpenter to make a wooden dummy gun for dry training. Four times a week, Shapath travelled from Meerut to the Karni Shooting Range in a Nano, studying in the back seat. Years later, that passion has taken him to the Asian Games, where he will represent India in trap shooting..Asian Games 2026 Live: Mixed recurve team enters semi-final Dhiraj Bommadevara and Kumkum Mohod continue their impressive run in the recurve mixed team event, defeating Vietnam 6-0 in the quarterfinal. The Indian pair advance to the semifinals after another dominant performance. Their mixed team campaign is now done for the day, but both archers will return in a few hours to compete in their respective men's and women's team events..Asian Games 2026 Live: Indian archers in form India make a strong start in the mixed team archery events, with both compound and recurve pairs advancing to the quarterfinals. In compound, Sahil Jadhav and Chikitha Taniparthi produce a flawless 160/160 against Mongolia, winning 160-146. They now face Kazakhstan, who also posted a perfect 160 against Chinese Taipei. In recurve, Dhiraj Bommadevara and Kumkum Mohod beat the UAE 6-0, scoring 37 points in each of the three sets. Their quarterfinal opponent is Vietnam, who defeat Iran 6-2.

articles.title: Sreeshankar, Solomon reach long jump final as Tejaswin slips to third in decathlon
articles.summary: Nagoya: Murali Sreeshankar and David Patturaj Solomon advanced to the men's long jump final at the ongoing Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Sunday, giving
articles.body: Nagoya: Murali Sreeshankar and David Patturaj Solomon advanced to the men's long jump final at the ongoing Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Sunday, giving India a double representation in the medal event.Sreeshankar finished second in Group B with a best effort of 7.84m. Solomon, meanwhile, secured third place in Group A after recording a best jump of 7.62m.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyIndia also had two athletes progress from the women's 400m hurdles heats, with Vithya Ramraj and Anu Raghavan both finishing second in their respective heats.Vithya clocked a season-best 55.73 seconds, while Anu produced a personal best of 55.84 seconds to book their places in the final.Tejaswin slips to thirdTejaswin Shankar dropped from first to third in the decathlon standings after the discus throw event on Sunday.He had entered the discus as the leader after finishing third in his 110m hurdles heat in 14.33 seconds, a performance that earned him 932 points. He was leading the overall standings with 5,270 points and appeared to be in contention for gold.However, Tejaswin finished third in the discus with a best throw of 36.77m, four metres short of his best. His overall tally moved to 5,869 points, leaving him third, with athletes from China and Japan occupying the top two positions.The final two events of the decathlon, the pole vault and javelin throw, are not exactly Tejaswin's strengths.Multiple exits in KurashIndia endured a difficult day in Kurash, with several athletes making early exits.Vishal was knocked out in the men's +90kg quarterfinals after a 0-5 loss to Thailand's Kunathip Yea-On.Sangita Balhara went down 10-0 to Charmea Quelino of the Philippines in her round-of-32 bout. Bharti then lost 3-0 to Iran's Tahereh Azarpeivand in the round of 16, while Yash Kumar suffered a 10-0 defeat to Tajikistan's Shakarmamad Mirmamadov.Manju sixth, Priyanka disqualifiedIndia's Manju Rani finished sixth in the women's marathon race walk, clocking 3:40:17.Priyanka Goswami, meanwhile, was disqualified after the 9km mark.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Ankush Panghal punches India’s first boxing medal with 5-0 quarterfinal win
articles.summary: Reigning Commonwealth Games champion Ankush Panghal delivered a commanding performance on Sunday to assure India of its first boxing medal at the Asian
articles.body: Reigning Commonwealth Games champion Ankush Panghal delivered a commanding performance on Sunday to assure India of its first boxing medal at the Asian Games 2026, defeating Tajikistan's Nekruz Salimov by a unanimous 5-0 decision in the men's 80kg quarterfinals.Ankush controlled the contest for most of the three rounds, using his speed, sharp combinations and solid defence to establish a decisive advantage before holding off a late challenge from Salimov.Ankush dominates first two roundsThe Indian boxer came out aggressively and immediately put Salimov under pressure with a combination of right hooks and crisp 1-2 punches. Ankush won the opening round unanimously, with all five judges scoring it in his favour. He continued to dictate the pace in the second round, showcasing his movement and counter-punching ability while making it difficult for Salimov to land clean shots.His powerful left hook proved particularly effective as he secured another 5-0 verdict in the second round, leaving the Tajik boxer needing a major turnaround in the final three minutes.Salimov fights back, but Ankush holds firmWith his tournament on the line, Salimov came out with greater urgency in the third round and looked to land heavier punches in search of a knockdown. The Tajik boxer managed to connect with a few shots and took the final round 4-1 on the judges' scorecards. However, Ankush had already built a comfortable lead and remained composed until the final bell.Four judges scored the bout 29-28 in Ankush's favour, while the fifth judge awarded him a 30-27 victory, completing a convincing 5-0 win. The quarterfinal victory guarantees Ankush at least a bronze medal, while the CWG champion will now turn his attention to the semifinals as he bids to go one step further.Kurash campaign ends for Indian athletesIndia's campaign in kurash, meanwhile, suffered a series of setbacks on Sunday. Vishal was knocked out in the men's +90kg quarterfinals after losing 5-0 to Thailand's Kunathip Yea-On.In the women's -57kg category, Sangita Balhara suffered a 10-0 defeat against the Philippines' Charmea Quelino in the Round of 32. Bharti was eliminated in the Round of 16 after losing to Iran's Tahereh Azarpeivand, while Yash Kumar Chauhan also exited the men's +90kg competition following a 10-0 defeat to Tajikistan's Shakarmamad Mirmamadov.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games: PV Sindhu, Unnati Hooda exits cap disappointing badminton campaign as India return with just one medal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s badminton campaign at the Asian Games 2026 ended on Sunday with a disappointing return of just one medal, as PV Sindhu and Unnati Hooda
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s badminton campaign at the Asian Games 2026 ended on Sunday with a disappointing return of just one medal, as PV Sindhu and Unnati Hooda bowed out in the women’s singles quarterfinals after spirited efforts against formidable opponents.Two-time Olympic medallist Sindhu went down 21-11, 18-21, 10-21 to Tokyo Olympic champion Chen Yu Fei of China, while 19-year-old Hooda pushed three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi of Japan before losing 16-21, 21-14, 17-21.The exits meant India failed to win a medal in any of the individual badminton events, with the men’s team bronze remaining the country’s only podium finish at Aichi-Nagoya. The contrast with the previous edition in Hangzhou was stark: India had won three medals there, including men’s team silver, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty’s doubles gold, and HS Prannoy’s singles bronze.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleSindhu fades after strong start against ChenSindhu, who had already played twice on Saturday, was competing for the third time in less than 24 hours. She started strongly against Chen, taking control of the opening game with sharp movement and aggressive shot-making to win it 21-11.The Indian also stayed in contention through much of the second game, which was closely fought and featured long rallies. The pair were level at 16-16 before Chen edged ahead to take the game 21-18 and force a decider.Chen seized control in the third, opening up an early lead and taking an 11-7 advantage at the interval. Sindhu managed only three more points after the break as the Chinese won 10 of the next 11 points to close out the match.Sindhu had entered the quarterfinal with a 7-9 head-to-head record against Chen, whom she had beaten on the way to winning the Japan Open Super 750 title in July. But the Indian could not repeat that result after a demanding schedule over the previous day.Hooda fights back but Yamaguchi holds onHooda also showed resilience in her quarterfinal against world No. 3 Yamaguchi, recovering from a one-sided opening game to take the second and force a decider.The Japanese controlled the early exchanges in the first game, using a range of strokes to build a sizeable lead and eventually take it 21-16. Hooda responded with a strong attacking display in the second, pulling level at 7-7 and then moving ahead as Yamaguchi began making errors. The Indian won eight successive points to claim the game 21-14.The decider remained tight, with the players level at 5-5 before Yamaguchi established a lead. Hooda continued to extend rallies and challenge the Japanese, but Yamaguchi held her advantage and closed out the match 21-17.Doubles pairs also fall in quarterfinalsIndia’s remaining doubles hopes had ended earlier on Sunday. Women’s pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, fresh from winning a maiden World Championships bronze last month, lost 18-21, 9-21 to Malaysia’s world No. 5 combination of Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan.In mixed doubles, Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto came close to upsetting the world No. 1 Chinese pair of Feng Yan Zhe and Huang Dongping, but eventually lost 14-21, 21-18, 18-21.Heavy schedule adds to players’ workloadThe demanding schedule was another talking point, with Sindhu, Hooda and Ayush Shetty among the players required to contest two matches within a few hours on Saturday. Sindhu’s quarterfinal against Chen was her third match in less than 24 hours, while Hooda also faced a taxing turnaround before her last-eight clash.Despite the effort and resilience shown by India’s leading shuttlers, the campaign ended well short of the three-medal return from Hangzhou. With only the men’s team bronze to show from Aichi-Nagoya, India’s badminton contingent leaves the Games without an individual-event medal.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: A's Have One More Game to Play Spoiler Against Houston
articles.summary: In addition to playing spoiler on Sunday, the A's will have an achievement of their own worth chasing.
articles.body:
The Athletics have been out of the hunt for October for weeks and will finish the season with the best odds of landing the No. 1 pick in the 2027 MLB Draft at 19.1%. That doesn't mean that they don't have something to play for on Sunday afternoon against the Houston Astros in the regular season finale.

With one game left, the Astros and Texas Rangers are tied atop the division with each team holding an 80-81 record. The Astros hold the tiebreaker over Texas, so a tie does the Rangers no good. That means Texas needs an A's win in order to have a shot at playing in October. They also need to win their own game to make that quest a reality.

A Houston win means they're in. A Texas loss eliminates the Rangers.

The A's will be going with all hands on deck on the mound. Seth Johnson will be serving as the team's opener, but Mark Kotsay has been adamant for weeks that his team wants to play spoiler. Sunday presents a key opportunity to end someone's season. It wouldn't be surprising to see the team empty out the bullpen chasing a win if one is within reach.

That's why Yunior Tur tossing the final 2 ⅓ innings and throwing 46 pitches on Saturday night could end up being a key factor on Sunday, as most of the primary relief options will have had a day off heading in, likely making them available for the final game.

The other thing the A's will be playing for is a bit of pride. Going into the series, they had a winning record against every team in the AL West. With Houston winning two of the first three games of this series, the Astros have evened up the season record at 6-6. A win on Sunday for the A's would put them back ahead 7-6 on the year.

The A's also held a 7-6 record against the Seattle Mariners and Rangers, and went 8-5 against the Angels . Despite holding a 64-97 record, holding a winning record against each team in the division would be one bright spot in an otherwise forgettable year.

Given the number of injuries the A's have faced this season and the lack of pitching needed to compete for much of the year, holding a winning record against each team in the division would be a huge confidence boost for the club going into next season when they will presumably be a bit healthier and have a little more pitching depth.

articles.title: USC has seen enough and it’s time to move on from Lincoln Riley
articles.summary: As Lincoln Riley walked off the field at the Coliseum on Saturday night after a 41-27 loss to Oregon, the result seemed much larger than the team’s first los...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — As Lincoln Riley walked off the field at the Coliseum on Saturday night after a 41-27 loss to Oregon , the result seemed much larger than the team's first loss of the season.

USC might be 4-1, but Trojans fans have seen this Riley production before, and they've lost interest in sticking around for the inevitable disappointing ending. The early victories create optimism. The first major disappointment comes with assurances that everything the team wants remains possible. Then the losses accumulate, and another season that began with playoff aspirations ends with everyone being asked to get excited about next year.

In 2025, USC started 4-0 before going 5-4 the rest of the season, culminating in a collapse against TCU in the Alamo Bowl. In 2024, USC started 3-1 before going 3-5 to finish the regular season. In 2023, USC started 6-0 before going 1-5 to finish the regular season.

Riley's high-water mark at USC remains his first season in 2022, and even that year offered a preview of what was coming. The Trojans lost to Utah in the Pac-12 championship game with the program's first College Football Playoff berth on the line, then blew a 15-point lead to Tulane in the final four minutes of the Cotton Bowl.

That history is why Saturday's fourth-quarter collapse felt so familiar. In his fifth season, Riley is still explaining why USC couldn't finish a game that could have changed how people view his program. At some point, those explanations become the strongest argument for finding someone else to lead it.

Riley is unlikely to be fired because of the Oregon loss, but USC should begin moving toward a future without him. There is too much evidence now to keep treating these performances as isolated disappointments on the way to something better.

The Trojans tied the game at 27 with 12:41 remaining when Jayden Maiava found Tanook Hines for an 11-yard touchdown. A sold-out crowd of 75,500 had every reason to believe this could finally be the night USC finished the job. The energy was there. The opportunity was there. Even Riley acknowledged afterward that the Coliseum had delivered everything his team could have wanted.

"That moment was probably the most rowdy I've heard our crowd since I've been here," Riley said. "It was a hell of an atmosphere in the Coliseum. We had all the momentum in the world."

Then USC did what it has done too often under Riley. It gave the opportunity away.

With Oregon facing third-and-15 from its own 40, an incomplete pass should have put the Trojans in position to get the ball back. Instead, a roughing-the-passer penalty against Jide Abasiri extended the possession. Oregon eventually scored on Dylan Raiola 's 29-yard touchdown pass to Dakorien Moore , and USC spent the rest of the night chasing a game it never caught.

The Trojans turned the ball over on downs at their own 49 on the next possession. Oregon then took 5:12 off the clock before Jordon Davison 's 2-yard touchdown run made it 41-27 with 2:03 remaining. After tying the score, USC allowed 14 unanswered points and never scored again.

The penalty mattered, but reducing this loss to one player's mistake would let the head coach off far too easily. USC surrendered 504 yards, failed to record a sack or force a turnover, and allowed Oregon to convert both of its fourth-down attempts. Riley's offense finished 2 for 11 on third down. There was plenty of responsibility to spread around.

Oregon also had to replace starting quarterback Dante Moore after USC linebacker Desman Stephens blasted him as he gave himself up and slid for a first down. Stephens was ejected for targeting but Riley allowed him to stay on USC's sideline even after celebrating the vicious cheap hit. Raiola came off the bench and completed 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns. USC couldn't take control against a team forced to make that adjustment on the road, in front of the loudest crowd Riley could remember during his tenure.

The Ducks were prepared to respond to adversity. USC was left explaining its response to opportunity.

"We had exactly what we wanted," Riley said. "But against good teams, if you give them opportunities to stay in the game or give them that fresh set of downs, it's tough to beat good teams that way."

He is right. He has also been here long enough for USC to expect a team that understands that before the postgame press conference. Discipline, tackling, communication and execution on critical downs are the head coach's responsibility. When those shortcomings keep deciding the biggest games, going back to work cannot be the entire answer.

The most revealing part of Riley's press conference came when he was asked about the evolution of his defense.

"I don't make big picture statements after a game," he said. "We just finished the game an hour ago."

He continued: "This is not about any of the games before. It's not about any of the games coming up. That's just a fantasy world. That's not what we live in."

Riley can ask his players to focus on the next practice and the next opponent. That is understandable. But USC cannot evaluate its head coach by pretending every Saturday exists independently of everything that came before it. The previous games are his record. The repeated collapses are his history. Looking at them together is how a university determines whether its football program is headed in the right direction.

The issues at USC run deeper than Riley, and replacing him won't automatically solve them. The university has to examine why it keeps finding itself here. But acknowledging institutional problems doesn't require keeping a coach who has failed to provide a convincing reason to believe the results will change.

Riley can still have success somewhere else. USC has seen that before. Pete Carroll won a Super Bowl after leaving. Ed Orgeron won a national championship at LSU . Lane Kiffin and Steve Sarkisian rebuilt their careers after humiliating exits. A coach's departure from USC doesn't have to be the end of his story, and the school doesn't have to keep waiting for his redemption to happen here.

On Saturday, Riley lost more than a game. He lost the trust of fans who had shown up ready to believe again, along with several boosters who hadn't texted me about the state of the program since Clay Helton was at the helm. Their frustration carried the exhaustion of people who have had this conversation too many times.

No one can know after five games exactly where this season will end. USC still has an opportunity to respond. But the burden should be on Riley to produce something different, not on everyone else to explain why they no longer expect it.

The Coliseum showed Saturday that the appetite for USC football is still there. Those fans want meaningful games, championship expectations and a reason to believe their program can meet the moment. They gave Riley another chance to show them that future against Oregon.

He gave them another reminder of the past. USC has waited long enough to turn the page.

articles.title: Marquez could benefit at any moment after Martin takes MotoGP injury gamble
articles.summary: MotoGP championship leader Jorge Martin has received a stark warning over his decision to opt against surgery. The Aprilia rider took the lead back from Marc...
articles.body:
MotoGP championship leader Jorge Martin has received a stark warning over his decision to opt against surgery.

The Aprilia rider took the lead back from Marc Marquez in Austria, a week on from arm pump taking him out of the battle in Misano.

Ahead of his impressive sprint victory and second place in the Grand Prix at the Red Bull Ring, Martin said he would decide on surgery the Monday after the weekend concluded.

However, with such a strong showing, he then admitted he didn't feel it was necessary, and that rest was the best option for his ailment.

Yet his vastly experienced agent, Carlo Pernat, has suggested the call could backfire at any moment.

Pernat has worked with a number of the sport's greats, and is more than familiar with how arm pump can strike at any moment.

Martin warned arm pump could occur without warning

Speaking to MotoSan, he said: "Martin has decided against surgery, and he probably made the right choice because the championship is very important to him.

"But he should be careful, because this compartment syndrome can strike suddenly, almost without warning, and the arm can become unusable.

"Regarding his choice, I would say that 50% of the decision is correct and 50% is incorrect. We'll see. I hope it was the right one…"

"It can strike suddenly, almost without warning, and the arm can become unusable."

Martin may have missed key window for operation

Arm pump is an issue almost every rider has experienced and is the colloquial term for chronic exertional compartment syndrome.

The issue is common in all forms of motorcycle racing and is alleviated by an insertion into the arm and removal of fascia.

Martin may have missed a key window for surgery , with a two-week break between Austria and Japan, followed by Indonesia a week later.

For Pernat, he now has only two title rivals, Marquez and Aprilia teammate Marco Bezzecchi.

Pernat names three riders in MotoGP title fight

He added: "This World Championship is being fought between three riders: Marquez, Martin, and Bezzecchi.

"It's a shame for Ai Ogura, who crashed a couple of times before his injury, but he showed what he's made of. And it's also a shame for Pedro [Acosta] , who crashed in the sprint when he could have accumulated another 12 points and closed the gap even further.

"Perhaps the World Championship wouldn't really have been decided, but it would have made everything even more interesting. It's truly a great world championship."

articles.title: Ayden Fernandez, strong defense power Reagan past Brandeis for first victory
articles.summary: The two-way athlete took on a bigger role as a running back to lead the Rattlers' offense as Reagan opened District 28-6A with a win over the Broncos.
articles.body:
Ayden Fernandez splits his time on both sides of the ball for Reagan, but the Rattlers turned to him to take on a bigger role on offense Saturday.

The two-way athlete rushed for 164 yards and two scores in leading Reagan to a 35-20 win over the Brandeis Broncos in a District 28-6A game at Farris Stadium.

Behind Fernandez's big rushing night and a defense which produced two interceptions returns for scores, Reagan (1-3, 1-0) picked up its first win of the season after losing its first three games. Most importantly, the Rattlers opened district play on the right note against Brandeis (2-2, 0-1), preserving a 7-0 record in the all-time series between the two teams.

Fernandez, a senior who also plays linebacker, said the improved Reagan rushing attack was the result of the work the offensive line has put in at practice.

"Our offensive line, these past two weeks we've been working on downhill run, downhill run, and that's what we did, downhill run," Fernandez said. "They can't stop it."

Reagan coach Preston Meyer said Fernandez is going to be seeing more time in the offensive backfield for the remainder of the season.

"If you're going to win football games, you got to be able to run the ball," Meyer said. "Ayden (Fernandez) had been playing some running back, but we decided let's give him a bigger role on the offensive side of the football. He can still play a little defense, but he's going to be our primary running back moving forward."

While Brandeis senior quarterback Wynter Smith rushed for 110 yards and one score, Reagan's defense limited the dual threat signal caller to 8-of-26 passing. Jayden Horace and Steven Robinson each returned interceptions for touchdowns for the Rattlers, and defensive end Emiliano Berlin sacked Smith twice.

"Well, we knew going into it, their quarterback would run around and make a lot of plays with his feet and with his arm," Meyer said. "But going into it, we knew if we could slow him down and give him trouble then we would be successful defensively. We knew you can't just go crazy, trying to bring pressure and rush him because he'll split you, and so we just wanted to keep the eyes on the quarterback, play some zone, underneath zone coverage. That way when he did try to escape, we had eyes on him ready to go, try to get him on the ground."

Reagan scored its first touchdown before its offensive unit got on the field, as Robinson picked off a Smith pass on the game's first possession, returning it 65 yards for the score with 8:29 left in the first quarter.

The Rattlers extended their lead to 14-0 late in the first quarter, as Fernandez scored his first touchdown on a 1-yarder, with sophomore Jayson Sinclair setting up Fernandez's score with a 32-yard scamper to the Brandeis 1-yard line.

Brandeis scored on two consecutive drives in the second quarter to tie the game at 14, first on a 26-yard scoring run from Smith, then on a 28-yard touchdown pass down the middle from Smith to sophomore Jacob De La O.

Reagan regained the lead on the ensuing possession. Quarterback Jace Huesser utilized the play-action fake to connect with tight end Russell Reed for a 72-yard touchdown catch with 3:27 remaining in the first half, giving the Rattlers a 21-14 halftime advantage.

Reagan struck quickly in the second half as Fernandez scored on a 43-yard run on the fourth play to put the Rattlers up by two touchdowns just over a minute into the third quarter.

Fernandez said his second touchdown run further boosted the energy level of his teammates.

"It was definitely energy once I scored," Fernandez said. "I came back on the sideline, everyone's up, it feels good. It 100 percent set the tone (for the rest of the game). After that we were firing, offense, special teams, defense and when a team is firing on all three phases, you can't beat them."

Brandeis chipped into the Reagan lead as Zach Cantu booted field goals of 41 and 49 yards on consecutive possessions to put the Broncos within 28-20 with 15 seconds left in the third quarter.

Reagan continued to grind it out on the ground in the second half, as Fernandez and Sinclair each carried the ball on a long drive that put the Rattlers at the Brandeis 11 in the fourth quarter. The drive set up a field goal attempt, but Brandeis blocked it to keep the game within one score.

But the momentum from the blocked field goal attempt would be short lived for the Broncos, as Reagan brought the pressure on Smith, whose pass was picked off by Horace for a 45-yard touchdown, sealing the win for the Rattlers with 6:13 left in the game.

images.caption: Reagan's Brody Beck moves the ball down the field during the first quarter of a District 28-6A game against Brandeis on Saturday, September 26, 2026 at Farris Stadium in San Antonio. (Charlie Blalock/For the Express-News)

articles.title: Former 76ers GM gives fans reason to be happy even when LeBron James, Joel Embiid ‘are out’
articles.summary: Former Sixers general manager Billy King explains that fans have something to look forward to even when their new superstar core misses time. The Philadelphi...
articles.body:
Former Sixers general manager Billy King explains that fans have something to look forward to even when their new superstar core misses time.

The Philadelphia 76ers have put together an incredible core. With Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey staying on the roster, the franchise has managed to add Jaylen Brown and LeBron James .

With a starting five that includes these four names, an NBA championship has become the expectation. However, there have been concerns about their ability to play many games together.

And now a former franchise executive has weighed in on the matter, discussing how fans won't be left high and dry even if the superstars can't play.

Billy King claims the Sixers' younger stars and bench can win games without Joel Embiid and LeBron James

The Philadelphia 76ers roster outside of the four stars and rookie sensation VJ Edgecombe has some interesting names. The team has added role players like Dean Wade , Kentavious Caldwell-Pope , and Anfernee Simons , among others.

That is not bad depth at all. They have physicality, shooting, and championship experience. Former franchise GM Billy King pointed this out when talking about the team recently.

"What they've done, is they've added some good bench pieces, which they never had here" King said about the Sixers. "The starting guys have been great but they didn't have enough depth.

"But they've added some good, young bench players. So when those guys are out… Say Joel and LeBron are out, you've still got a squad with Jaylen, VJ, Maxey, and the bench pieces they have added.

"So I think that team will have a chance to really continue to win when those guys are out."

King did say that the superstars would have to ultimately be healthy if the Sixers are to win. But his point about the bench situation is valid. If the 76ers have any two of their Big 4 on the court with the rest of the roster, they will still be in good shape against anyone.

articles.title: ‘Won’t last…’ Giants fans worried about Cam Skattebo after he shows shoulder issue during stream
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo revealed the physical impact of playing football on his shoulder, and fans are worried the New York Giants’ future may have just gone from bad t...
articles.body:
Cam Skattebo revealed the physical impact of playing football on his shoulder, and fans are worried the New York Giants ' future may have just gone from bad to worse.

The Giants have already lost Jaxson Dart to a season-ending knee surgery, forcing John Harbaugh to rely on Jameis Winston as their starting quarterback for the rest of the year.

But if Skattebo's injury is as bad as it looks, Giants fans have even more reason to be concerned about their prospects not just this year, but for many years going forward.

Cam Skattebo's shoulder has fans concerned about his future

During a livestream, New York Giants RB Cam Skattebo revealed the impact years of playing football have had on his shoulder.

He moved his sweatshirt to show a massive bump on his shoulder joint that is so sharp that he can use it to scratch his chin.

"Chat, I've got a twin right here. I scratch my chin with this."

Understandably, fans were very concerned about the way Skattebo's shoulder looks, with many suggesting that his career could be cut short by this.

One fan wrote, "AC separation. I have one too. From snowboarding….. I'm done snowboarding."

Another fan added, "That's not supposed to do that!"

A third fan shared his concern, noting, "Does bro have a broken collarbone and just acting like it's no big deal? Holy c***."

"He gonna be 35 begging to be shut down," wrote a fourth fan detailing the impact this injury could have had on his long-term career.

A fifth fan noted, "He won't last," admitting that Skattebo's injury could cut his career short.

And lastly, one fan pointed out how his injury serves as a contrast to another great NFL RB, saying, "It took Keenan Allen almost ten years in the league to grow his."

Clearly, Skattebo has suffered many shoulder injuries during his career, and his injuries have taken a huge toll on his body.

It is possible that these injuries could have a significant impact on his career and possibly cut his career short.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: What Indian medallists can earn in cash rewards, government jobs and state incentives
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s medal winners at the Asian Games 2026 could return home with more than a place on the podium.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s medal winners at the Asian Games 2026 could return home with more than a place on the podium. Along with national recognition, athletes who win gold, silver or bronze are eligible for cash awards under a central government scheme. They may also qualify for sports-quota jobs and additional incentives announced by their respective state governments.The central cash awards are laid out in the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports’ “Special Awards to Medal Winners in International Sports Events and their Coaches” scheme. The scheme, first introduced in 1986, has been revised over time, with the stated aim of rewarding sporting achievement, encouraging higher performance and inspiring young people to take up sports.For an individual Asian Games medal, the listed central award is Rs 30 lakh for gold, Rs 20 lakh for silver and Rs 10 lakh for bronze. These are the base figures: the amount for a team medal depends on the size of the team and the scheme’s rules for calculating and distributing awards.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleHow much does an individual medallist receive?Under the central scheme, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games medal awards are the same. Olympic medal awards are higher.CompetitionGoldSilverBronzeOlympic GamesRs 75 lakhRs 50 lakhRs 30 lakhAsian GamesRs 30 lakhRs 20 lakhRs 10 lakhCommonwealth GamesRs 30 lakhRs 20 lakhRs 10 lakhThe same corresponding award amounts apply to Para Games medal winners. The cash incentive is subject to the eligibility criteria and conditions prescribed by the government.That means an Indian athlete who wins an individual gold in Aichi-Nagoya could be eligible for a central award of Rs 30 lakh. A silver medallist’s listed award is Rs 20 lakh, while a bronze medallist’s is Rs 10 lakh.Team medals: the calculation changesFor team events, the scheme determines the award using the number of athletes in the team on the ground. The multiplier is applied to the corresponding individual-event award for the competition, medal and category.A team of two receives 1.5 times the corresponding award; a team of three or four receives twice the award; a team of five to 10 receives three times the award; and a team with more than 10 members receives five times the award. The resulting amount is shared equally among the team members, with a condition that no member receives less than 50% of the corresponding individual-event award.The scheme defines team events as competitions in which athletes compete collectively, and says incentives are awarded to all team members, including bench or reserve players, in accordance with the international standards applicable to each sport. It also provides that, in specified sports disciplines, each team member’s cash incentive is 75% of the incentive amount applicable to the corresponding individual event, based on the medal, level and participation category.These provisions mean that a team medal cannot simply be treated as the same flat award for every athlete. The final amount depends on the event’s classification, team strength and applicable scheme provisions.Multiple medals and the highest-award ruleThe scheme also addresses athletes who win more than one medal at an international event. As a general rule, a sportsperson who wins multiple medals in individual or team categories is eligible for the cash incentive only for the highest-ranking medal won at that event.There is an important exception for the Olympic Games, Paralympic Games, Asian Games and Para-Asian Games: athletes who win multiple medals in individual or team categories may be eligible for the cash incentive for each medal, subject to the scheme’s terms and conditions.For an Asian Games athlete who wins more than one medal, therefore, the central award may be calculated medal by medal rather than being limited to the single highest finish. The precise amount still depends on whether the medals were won individually or as part of a team, and on the applicable team-event rules.The figures and provisions above are from the Department of Sports, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports circular dated January 31, 2025, as provided in the scheme details.Can Asian Games medallists get government jobs?Cash awards are only one part of the potential support available to medal winners. Athletes who have represented India in recognised international competitions, including the Asian Games, may also be considered for recruitment under sports-quota provisions.At the central level, recruitment of meritorious sportspersons is governed by Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) instructions and related office memorandums. The central framework generally provides for appointment to Group C and erstwhile Group D posts, subject to eligibility, recruitment rules and the specific terms in force. It does not establish a general entitlement for every medal winner to receive a Group A or Group B post.A medal does not, by itself, mean that a job is automatically granted. Athletes must meet the relevant conditions, and appointments depend on the applicable recruitment process and rules. Serving government employees may also be covered by separate provisions, including certain out-of-turn promotion or incentive arrangements, where permitted.State incentives can add another layerThe amount an athlete may receive after the Games can vary further because state governments frame their own sports policies and service rules. Some states offer additional cash awards, employment opportunities or other incentives to athletes from their state who win medals at major international competitions.As a result, two Indian athletes who win the same medal at the Asian Games may be eligible for different overall benefits depending on their state’s policy and their individual circumstances. State incentives are not uniform across India, and any announced reward or job offer must be checked against the specific state’s policy, eligibility conditions and formal government orders.For athletes and families assessing what a medal could mean financially, the key distinction is between the central scheme’s published cash award and any separate state-level benefit. The central award schedule gives a clear starting point – Rs 30 lakh, Rs 20 lakh and Rs 10 lakh for individual Asian Games gold, silver and bronze – but the final package may depend on team-event calculations, multiple-medal provisions, state rules and eligibility for recruitment or other incentives.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Virat Kohli score today in India vs. West Indies 1st ODI in Thiruvananthapuram
articles.summary: Follow Virat Kohli's score today in the India vs West Indies 1st ODI at Thiruvananthapuram. Get runs scored, balls faced, and boundary counts.
articles.body:
Virat Kohli is back in action for Team India and will take the field once again on Sunday as the Men in Blue take on West Indies in the first of the three-match ODI series in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala

Kohli last played for India against England at Lord's, where he played a brilliant knock of 74 runs but missed out on his 86th international century. Kohli's wicket proved costly as India narrowly missed out on a historic 387-run chase by 27 runs.

Kohli, along with another former India captain, Rohit Sharma, is preparing for the ODI World Cup, which is only a year from now.

The veteran stars, who now play only in the ODI format, will see the upcoming World Cup as their last dance and would hope to end their memorable journey as a cricketer on a bright note and lift the elusive trophy.

In the series against West Indies, Virat Kohli will also look to break three key records held by Sachin Tendulkar, which include most international centuries and most international runs in home conditions.

Virat Kohli is expected to come out first down in the ODI against West Indies.

articles.title: College Football Rankings Week 5: Possibly Our Craziest Top 25 Yet
articles.summary: We're not happy about the latest CFN Top 25 rankings, but for now, this is how we have to do them going into Week 5. We're sorry.
articles.body:
Before you go one step further with the Week 5 CFN Top 25, please understand one extremely important disclaimer: We don't like our rankings this week, either. There's a Grand Canyon-sized glitch happening at the moment, and there's just no way around it until next week, at least – Tulsa beat Oklahoma State 24-10 in Week 1 (and it wasn't some last-second Hail Mary thing). We've done our rankings the same way ever since we started in 1998 – always go by what happened on the field, regardless of school name, beliefs, or hype, and then, as the season goes on, there's a combination of Respect The Results along with our sane and rational judgment. So please, be kind, understand that we totally get it, and yes, there will be massive changes coming soon.

CFN Week 5 Top 25 Teams: It Has To Be This Way, For Now

Record: (3-1) Last Week Rank: 38 Week 4: Oregon 41, USC 27 Up Next: OPEN DATE And here's our problem. We want to rank Oregon because it really is one of the 25 best teams in college football – and, honestly, when it's humming, it probably belongs in the top five. We also want to give the Ducks credit for beating USC, but there's a problem with that, too – USC's wins were against San Jose State, Fresno State, Louisiana, and it struggled against a lousy Rutgers team that got whacked by UMass. Trade the USC name for, say, Purdue, with the same sort of resume and results, and the win wouldn't be that big of a deal. But to rank Oregon means we have to respect the 39-31 loss to a 3-1 Oklahoma State team that we also want to rank, so …

Record: (3-1) Last Week Rank: 37 Week 4: Oklahoma State 41, West Virginia 24 Up Next: OPEN DATE The win over West Virginia in Morgantown was fantastic. The Cowboys are up to speed, looking great over the last three weeks against the Mountaineers, Murray State, and, of course, Oregon. So to do this correctly – for now – we must rank the Cowboys ahead of the Ducks, which means we (seriously, we're holding our noses here) have to rank …

Record: (3-1) Last Week Rank: 36 Week 4: Arkansas 34, Tulsa 6 Up Next: North Texas Again, Tulsa stuffed this Cowboy team in Week 1 in a 24-10 win, and it was even more impressive than you might think. The Golden Hurricane were up 17-3 late in the third, forced four turnovers, and were only outgained by seven yards. So for now, Tulsa has to be ranked higher than Oklahoma State, which means – and hold on to your butts on this …

Record: (2-2) Last Week Rank: 75 Week 4: Arkansas 34, Tulsa 6 Up Next: at Texas A&M Before you holler at us, remember who the two Arkansas losses were against. Georgia, who might win the national title, and Utah, who might at least win the Big 12 Championship. Those two are destroying everyone, not just Arkansas, who just blew out Tulsa, making this the hardest piece of the puzzle to fit. And with that, the top 21 becomes a tad more normal.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 55 Week 4: Cincinnati 31, Kansas State 26 Up Next: at Arizona After screaming from the rooftops for the last six months that Kansas State was terrific, now we have to give the just-due credit to the team that beat the team we liked so much. Also, Washington State put up a fight against Washington and Arizona, and got whacked by the Bearcats by 27.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 43 Week 4: Nebraska 31, Michigan State 13 Up Next: Maryland It would be nice to have a stronger top win than Michigan State, but it was on the road – it beat the Spartans by more than Notre Dame did. Somewhat quietly, the Huskers have four double-digit blowout wins to start the season, and there will probably be a fifth next week against Maryland before hosting Indiana.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 26 Week 4: Virginia Tech 21, Boston College 14 Up Next: Pitt This falls into the "prove it, already" category, but we liked James Franklin's team all offseason, and it's getting the job done in workmanlike fashion so far. Now it has to beat an unbeaten Pitt team.

Record: (3-1) Last Week Rank: 19 Week 4: Iowa 20, Michigan 19 Up Next: at Minnesota The defense is so good that this bunch can hang with just about anyone, and the offense is so blah that we realize this is way too high. Don't blow off the Oklahoma win just because the Sooners got rocked by an amazing Georgia team; that was still a strong victory. But like Virginia Tech, there's a prove-it thing happening here. Go win the Little Brown Jug game at Minnesota next week, and the respect will follow.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 22 Week 4: Texas Tech 49, Sam Houston 14 Up Next: at Colorado We should probably be giving more respect to the win over Houston two weeks ago, but overall, this schedule is just so … meh. The team hasn't looked like last year's version, but 4-0 doesn't care where 4-0 came from.

Record: (3-0) Last Week Rank: 18 Week 4: OPEN DATE Up Next: at TCU The Arizona win deserves respect, and the 41-23 victory at Colorado State should've been by more. Next week's date at TCU will be interesting. If the Cougars are all that, they should roll.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 25 Week 4: UCLA 54, Maryland 3 Up Next: OPEN DATE Just when it became concerning that the defense couldn't slow down Purdue, and there might be issues … BOOM. It shut down a high-powered Maryland team in College Park, and once again, the ground attack was incredible. There still isn't an amazing win, but after a week off comes a trip to Oregon.

Record: (3-1) Last Week Rank: 12 Week 4: Texas 20, Tennessee 17 Up Next: Auburn Forgetting the clown show that was the final 90 seconds, Tennessee had a throw into the end zone that wasn't terribly far off from beating the No. 1 team in America. This team is still really good.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 33 Week 4: Iowa 20, Michigan 19 Up Next: Ohio State For just about anyone else, the eye-test would keep the Hawkeyes from coming anywhere near this high – you and ten friends could slow down the Michigan offense. But that's how this bunch works. Great defense, special teams, stay in the game, and when there's a chance to do something special, do it. (Now do something special and don't get doornailed by Ohio State.)

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 20 Week 4: Mississippi State 31, Missouri 24 Up Next: Alabama Minnesota went to Washington and handed the Huskies their first defeat. When Mississippi State beat the Gophers, at the time that was more about how bad Minnesota was, when in reality, the 38-13 domination on the road showed how good the Bulldogs were, and they proved it with wins over South Carolina and Missouri.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 11 Week 4: Utah 28, Iowa State 20 Up Next: OPEN DATE The win over an okay Iowa State team could've been a bit more impressive, but that's what the Cyclones do – they play close games. Utah obliterated that Arkansas team that beat Tulsa, that beat … (sorry, too soon … too soon …)

Record: (3-1) Last Week Rank: 6 Week 4: LSU 35, Texas A&M 6 Up Next: McNeese Again, we don't like our own top 25 this week. Really, LSU is probably one of the five best teams in America – especially in Baton Rouge – but if we're going to set the dial to full pretentiousness, then yeah, for now we have to rank the Tigers behind Ole Miss after the loss two weeks ago.

Record: (3-1) Last Week Rank: 5 Week 4: Florida 52, Ole Miss 28 Up Next: OPEN DATE Florida appears to be just that amazing, and Ole Miss seemed a tad fried after the overblown hype around the Lane Kiffin/LSU game. The schedule ahead is a bear, but the Rebels did beat LSU, and Trinidad Chambliss is still amazing.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 8 Week 4: Indiana 29, Northwestern 23 Up Next: at Rutgers This is a total gift considering how sloppy the defending national champs were against Northwestern. After starting the season with three cream puffs, there was no excuse to struggle that much. Let's just say Curt Cignetti has earned the benefit of a few hundred doubts.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 9 Week 4: Miami 52, Central Michigan 3 Up Next: at Clemson It's been lost in the weeds, but don't blow off the 33-20 win at Wake Forest a few weeks ago. The Demon Deacons have been fabulous, including a great win over Louisville this week. The date at Clemson should be an interesting measuring stick.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 14 Week 4: Florida 52, Ole Miss 28 Up Next: at Missouri You hang 44 at Auburn and follow it up with a dominant win over the team that just handed that LSU team a loss, and you're doing something right. The defense might still need some reworking, but Jon Sumrall's team is humming offensively.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 7 Week 4: Alabama 49, South Carolina 18 Up Next: at Mississippi State It was 35-3 in the first half against a South Carolina team with the talent to – at least in the minds of some – pull off the upset. It's time to put Keelon Russell deep into the Heisman conversation.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 4 Week 4: Georgia 41, Oklahoma 13 Up Next: Vanderbilt No one really wants to believe this, but Oklahoma is actually good, and Georgia just ran over it like it was a light scrimmage. If you want to say this is the No. 1 team in America right now based on the way its playing, no argument here.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 3 Week 4: Notre Dame 49, Purdue 10 Yeah, yeah, yeah, it was against Purdue, but it was 35-0 before anyone could get comfortable. And all of a sudden, that 41-13 win over Wisconsin looks even better. If anything, we all might be undervaluing that this is it. This is the best team in America, and it's going to blast through everything in its path.

Record: (3-1) Last Week Rank: 2 Week 4: Ohio State 42, Illinois 19 Like we said last week, the kid hits the field goal attempt straight late in the game at Texas, and Ohio State is the unquestioned No. 1 team in America. Jeremiah Smith is terrifyingly great.

Record: (4-0) Last Week Rank: 1 Week 4: Texas 20, Tennessee 17 Give credit to a Texas team that had to scratch and claw its way to pull off a win against Ohio State, and got through a rock fight at Tennessee when things weren't working quite right. We all know how talented this team is, but it's got grit.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic has advice to give Iga Swiatek and promises they’ll talk more soon
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic may be 39 years of age with his powers waning, yet he remains one of tennis’ most integral and influential figures of all...
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic may be 39 years of age with his powers waning, yet he remains one of tennis' most integral and influential figures of all time.

Even today, as results may not be going his way, the Serbian is still a vital port of call for many of the sport's best players, with Iga Swiatek the latest to request his help.

Felix Auger-Aliassime, Joao Fonseca and Iva Jovic are three notable stars to have benefitted from his advice, whilst last year, Darren Cahill even attributed some of Sinner's success to advice Djokovic gave back in 2022.

The impact he has had on tennis goes far beyond the many, many trophies and accolades he has amassed.

Swiatek could be the latest set to enjoy an upturn in form because of his genius.

Iga Swiatek seeks advice from Novak Djokovic in Beijing

Djokovic's physio recently stated that he loves helping young players to improve their games, but Swiatek is hardly that.

She is no newcomer seeking a breakthrough moment; this is a six-time Grand Slam champion, who is just one Australian Open title away from completing the Career Grand Slam.

So, it arguably makes her request for his advice even more powerful, with one great champion bowing to another's superior experience and quality.

From the footage that emerged, it appeared that the Polish star was seeking counsel on her return position.

Novak Djokovic was heard noting: "As I said, I have a bit more wide like this, I try to have the feet open a little bit, I try to open a little bit more because… but it has evolved. When I was younger, I was standing a little more like this (bent over forward). Now, and then before, maybe five, six years ago, I was here (leaning back slightly). And now I'm here (middle ground stance). So, it's evolving."

He then added: "We'll talk more. My coach is already, I feel, here (gestures to the back of his neck). A lot of pressure."

Swiatek thanked him, and Djokovic insisted it was 'no problem'.

Djokovic, meanwhile, is set to make his first appearance since losing in the first round of the US Open late last month.

articles.title: Joe Cullen comments on the defensive line's growth ahead of Week 3
articles.summary: During his press conference, Kansas City Chiefs defensive line coach Joe Cullen commented on the defensive line's growth ahead of Week 3 | @EdEastonJr
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs defensive line coach Joe Cullen spoke recently with reporters. He commented on the defensive line's growth ahead of Week 3 against the Miami Dolphins .

"Well, I tell you, we're stout, we're physical, and we grind, and that's the thing that's been really good. The first run of the Denver game, Chris (Jones) knocked the guard back about three yards, and Felix (Anudike-Uzomah) came down the line of scrimmage; no gain. And one squirted out in that game," said Cullen. "Then last week, it's as good a back as there is. I wish we had a couple back, that one right before the half. But we really had to nail it down, all 11 it takes to stop the run. But the guys keep grinding, and they're getting better with the technique."

Players such as Felix Anudike-Uzomah and R Mason Thomas have stood out in early-season games. The defense had plenty of standout plays in the Week 1 win over the Denver Broncos , but pressure dipped slightly in Week 2 against the Indianapolis Colts . Cullen will keep expectations high for his group on the road against a struggling Miami Dolphins team.
